The nbfx Status API defines the annotation with which a module contributes an element to the JavaFX status bar.
The module contains the SOURCE-retention @StatusRegistration annotation, the StatusAlignment enum and a LayerGeneratingProcessor that writes NbFx/Status entries into the compiling module's generated layer. The status bar reader consumes those entries through LayerPaths.
A module declares a status bar element with @StatusRegistration; the generated layer supplies its id, alignment and position to the status bar.
The processor is covered by a unit test that asserts the generated layer fragment for a sample annotated source. The module API is marked under development until the MVP freeze, after which API signature tests (sigtest) are enabled.
A JDK is required to compile the annotation processor.
Only com.gluonhq.netbeans.nbfx.api.status is public. The processor implementation is an implementation detail and is not exported.
The processor is discovered by the compiler through the META-INF/services/javax.annotation.processing.Processor service, generated by @ServiceProvider(service=Processor.class).
See lookup-lookup.
Yes. The processor creates NbFx/Status/<id>.instance entries.

The annotation processor runs in the compiler's processing rounds and is stateless. It does not touch the JavaFX thread.
No code runs on startup; the module only contributes a compiled annotation processor.
